profile.campus: Stanton Springs, Newton County, Georgia (Meta's Stanton Springs data center campus, roughly 40 miles east of Atlanta)
profile.reading:
This building is Meta's Stanton Springs data center (formerly called the Newton Data Center), located in the Stanton Springs development in Newton County, Georgia, about 40 miles east of downtown Atlanta near Social Circle. Facebook announced the project with $750 million in investment for a two-building, 970,000-square-foot campus, and Data Center Frontier reported the facility was fully operational by 2020; at the time of Meta's own March 2021 announcement recapping the project, it was described as Meta's 12th data center globally and 9th in the United States. Meta secured 100% renewable power for the site through a partnership with Walton Electric Membership Corporation, which committed to installing hundreds of megawatts of new solar generation on the Georgia grid to match the facility's electricity use, part of what a Meta representative described as a "renewable energy solution" and "strong partners" being key to the site-selection process. Meta's own materials describe an economic multiplier of roughly 5 jobs supported elsewhere in the local economy per data center job, and about 14.5 jobs per $1 million of capital expenditure, alongside hundreds of construction and trades jobs during the building phase and ongoing engineering and facility-management roles. The site joined a broader hyperscale cluster in the region alongside Switch and CyrusOne, both of which have also expanded data center operations in the same part of Georgia. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage; the 970,000-square-foot figure is a campus-wide total across two buildings, not confirmed per building, and the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates rather than an operator-published source.

Meta's current fact sheet-level materials for its Georgia operations describe the same standard LEED Gold, net-zero, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments applied across its US campuses, alongside the Walton EMC renewable partnership described above as central to why Meta selected the Stanton Springs site.

reading.body:
Meta's Stanton Springs data center in Newton County, Georgia, comprises two buildings totaling 970,000 square feet that reached full operation in 2020. The facility was built with a $750 million capital commitment and Meta announced it as its 12th data center globally and 9th in the United States at the time of opening. Meta does not publish the specific megawatt capacity of this campus, so its absolute size relative to AI training demand cannot be read from operator specifications.

The site secured a renewable power partnership with Walton Electric Membership Corporation, which committed to installing hundreds of megawatts of new solar generation to match the facility's electricity use. This arrangement was material to Meta's site selection and represents a direct model for pairing hyperscale demand to regional grid expansion. Stanton Springs sits within a central Georgia data center corridor that includes facilities operated by Switch and CyrusOne, making the region a mapped cluster of 33 hyperscale data center sites statewide.

Georgia's four facilities with published megawatt figures report a combined 66.3 MW of capacity, of which this campus does not constitute one. Stanton Springs therefore ranks unspecified by the only metric this site measures: it holds the technical footprint and the renewable power commitment of a hyperscale AI-era facility, but the operator has chosen not to disclose the megawatts that would place it in the published ranking.
